claims.statement: Chatbot-supported L2 instruction has a positive average effect on learning outcomes, but effects are heterogeneous and vary with modality, mobility, generative-AI use and comparison conditions.
claims.limitations: Meta-analyses aggregate many tools, learner populations and outcomes; average effects do not validate a particular Nếp AI feature.

claims.statement: Current empirical GenAI language-learning research is concentrated in higher education, EFL and writing, with limited longitudinal evidence and substantially less coverage of listening, reading and lower-proficiency populations.
claims.limitations: The field is changing rapidly, so the evidence distribution itself can shift with new studies.

claims.statement: GenAI can serve useful pedagogical roles such as tutor, feedback provider, content generator and conversation partner, but reported challenges include content-quality failures, querying difficulty, overreliance, pedagogical limitations and integrity concerns.
claims.limitations: Role labels cover heterogeneous implementations and do not imply equal validity across roles.

claims.statement: Automated written feedback research shows mixed results and comparatively limited validation evidence, so usefulness or learner acceptance should not be treated as evidence that automated feedback correctly diagnoses every writing problem.
claims.limitations: Most reviewed systems predate or differ from current frontier LLMs; the evidence is writing-specific.

claims.statement: LLM writing raters can achieve useful reliability and validity under some prompts, models and rubrics, but performance varies across models and over time and does not justify assuming stable rater behavior.
claims.limitations: The studies concern essay assessment and relatively structured scoring contexts, not Nếp’s full set of beginner constructs.

claims.statement: LLM assessment quality depends on the criterion: narrow or explicitly specified criteria can be more consistent than diagnostic, holistic or subjective judgments, and detailed rubrics can improve but not eliminate reliability problems.
claims.limitations: Findings depend on the exact model, prompt, rubric and sample; they do not define a universal hierarchy of scorable constructs.

claims.statement: High precision among issues an LLM chooses to flag does not establish complete error detection; an AI system can provide mostly correct feedback while still missing learner problems or misclassifying some issues.
claims.limitations: Direct evidence is primarily L2 writing; equivalent recall/coverage properties must be tested separately in other modalities.

claims.statement: Human–chatbot comparison studies suggest chatbots can provide language-practice benefits comparable to humans in some linguistic outcomes, while humans retain advantages in some socially interactive and sustained-interpersonal dimensions.
claims.limitations: Only 11 experimental studies were included and chatbot technology evolves quickly; this does not define all human-versus-AI differences.

claims.statement: Modern synthetic speech can be sufficiently comprehensible or yield performance comparable to human recordings in some controlled EFL learning and listening-assessment tasks.
claims.limitations: Comparability is task-, voice-, text- and population-specific and does not establish equivalence to natural speech in general.

claims.statement: Synthetic speech can differ from natural speech in naturalness, intelligibility and listening effort, and these differences can become consequential for non-native listeners or adverse listening conditions.
claims.limitations: TTS technology changes rapidly and the cited studies use particular synthesis systems and learner populations.

claims.statement: Success with TTS-supported listening cannot by itself establish transfer to natural human speech, because source type is part of the listening condition and can alter the perceptual task.
claims.limitations: This is a construct-validity synthesis; direct TTS-training-to-unseen-natural-speech transfer studies remain limited.

claims.statement: Success in AI-mediated conversation is supported interaction evidence rather than proof of human-interaction capability, because chatbot interlocutors can differ from humans in interactivity, elaboration and social-pragmatic demands.
claims.limitations: The degree of AI accommodation varies by model and prompt and must be measured directly in Nếp.

claims.statement: Commercial LLM services can exhibit substantial behavioral and performance drift across model versions or time, including changes in instruction-following, so a previously validated prompt-model configuration cannot be assumed valid indefinitely.
claims.limitations: Observed drift does not identify the provider-side causal mechanism and may differ across modern models and tasks.

claims.statement: Privacy, data protection, bias, transparency, cognitive autonomy and accountability are recurring risks in educational GenAI deployment and require operational governance rather than relying on model capability alone.
claims.limitations: Much ethics literature is higher-education focused and combines empirical and normative evidence; exact Nếp controls require product-specific threat and privacy analysis.

claims.statement: For Nếp, AI output should be interpreted according to a declared role and validated scope, with exact provenance and fail-closed gates before AI output can influence durable learner evidence.
claims.limitations: This is a product synthesis and must be validated operationally; overly strict gating can add cost or reduce useful feedback.

claims.statement: The safe provider/model mix, prompt and rubric versions, feedback confidence thresholds, TTS voice policy, human or deterministic escalation rate, privacy policy and revalidation cadence for Vietnamese near-A0/A1 learners are not established and require direct experimentation.
